title: Amara Theme
description: Framework-agnostic token schema for an AI agent/chatbot UI system. Three layers: primitive (raw values) -> semantic (purpose-mapped) -> component (surface-specific refs). Generators consume this file to emit React/Tailwind, plain HTML/CSS/JS, or chat-widget SDK theme configs.

meta.description: Identity of the generated system. designPrinciple is mandatory and must be stated before any token decisions are made -- every token in this file should be traceable back to it.

styleFamily.description: Where on the style spectrum this system sits, e.g. 'Minimalist/Swiss', 'Claymorphism', 'Brutalism/Neo-brutalism'. See styles/ for the full taxonomy.

designPrinciple.description: 2-3 sentence statement generated early and used to accept/reject every later decision. Not decorative copy -- an actual constraint.

removedElement.description: What was deliberately cut from the first draft during the QA pass. Required by the self-critique loop; a non-empty value is evidence restraint was actually applied, not assumed.

generatedFrom.description: Provenance of the input that produced this theme -- which input modes were used and how they were blended.

referenceDescription.description: If mode included 'reference': a description of the STYLE CHARACTERISTICS extracted (weight, proportion, rhythm, palette feel) -- never the source's literal name used as a brand claim, never copied assets.

overridesApplied.description: Dot-paths of fields the user pinned directly, bypassing inference (e.g. 'color.primitive.accent.500', 'components.approvalBanner.elevation').

color.description: Three-layer color system. Always define both light and dark. Every semantic pairing must pass WCAG AA before this file is considered valid -- see a11y.contrastReport.

harmonyModel.description: See references/color-theory.md for which models suit which style families.

distributionRatio.description: 60/30/10 dominant/secondary/accent sanity check, expressed as approximate area percentage. Applies even in maximalist palettes -- 'more colors' is not exempt from 'one thing dominates'.

primitive.description: Raw color scales, unassigned to purpose. Each scale is a 50-900 ramp.

semantic.description: Purpose-mapped tokens, each a reference to a primitive scale step (e.g. 'primitive.primary.600'), not a raw hex.

approvalRequired.description: Reserved color that must not be reused elsewhere in the system -- see agent-states.md on why the approval banner needs an uncontested color.

dark.description: Full parallel semantic map for dark mode. Not a filter over light values -- generated and contrast-checked independently.

scaleRatio.description: Type scale ratio. Max 4-5 distinct sizes system-wide, all derived from this ratio off a base size -- no off-scale one-offs.

messageBody.description: Can differ from ui for a real typographic pairing -- avoid defaulting both to the same grotesque.

monospace.description: Code blocks and fallback for structured/tabular agent output.

scale.description: Ordered size steps, each traceable to base * scaleRatio^n.
All spacing in the system must be a multiple drawn from this array -- no arbitrary values.

iconTier.description: See references/motion-icon-tiers.md. 'gif' requires explicit opt-in and a documented warning; 'video-loop' should almost never be chosen for a widget.

reducedMotion.description: Non-optional fallback per animated element -- required even for gif/video tiers, where it typically means 'freeze on first frame'.

styleDescriptor.description: e.g. 'rounded, 1.5px stroke, no fill' -- a written spec so any icon added later stays consistent.

setReference.description: Name of an icon set consistent with styleDescriptor (e.g. 'Phosphor Regular', 'Lucide'), not bundled assets.

avatar.description: The agent's persona mark, modeled as a state machine -- never a single static image.

components.description: Component-layer tokens: each field is a reference into semantic/primitive tokens plus layout constants, never a new raw value.

presenceIndicator.description: online / working-in-background / asleep. Distinct from thinkingVsDoing.

thinkingVsDoing.description: Visual distinction between 'model is reasoning' and 'agent is taking an action' (tool call, API request). Must read as two different things at a glance.

approvalBanner.description: Must out-rank every other element on screen when present -- highest elevation token, reserved color, motion used once on entry only (not looping).

activityLog.description: Optional transparency log of agent actions.

errorState.description: Must read as trustworthy, not alarming -- see agent-states.md.

elevationScale.description: Ordered z-axis/shadow steps, reused everywhere rather than invented per component. bubble < input bar < approvalBanner.

contrastMode.description: AA is the floor, not a toggle. Generation that fails AA is rejected and regenerated, never shipped with a caveat.

contrastReport.description: Every text/background pairing checked, with pass/fail. Produced by the QA pass -- see references/qa-checklist.md.

readingOrder.description: Note on DOM/ARIA order vs visual order, for RTL and screen readers.

resources.description: Optional. Pointers to the actual open-source/free assets that realize this system's tokens -- see references/resource-library.md. Each field is independently swappable via the targeted-override syntax (input-modes.md #4): changing resources.iconSet does not require regenerating anything else. Omitting this block entirely is valid -- an adapter should fall back to the resource-library.md defaults for the chosen style family rather than treat it as an error.

uiKit.description: Per-framework component-kit pick for whichever output adapter is in use -- only populate the target(s) actually requested.

resourceRef.description: One resource-library pick. license uses the same key as resource-library.md: OSI (real open-source license), OFL (SIL Open Font License), CC0 (public domain), Free (no-cost but not open-source -- check redistribution terms), or Freemium (free tier of a proprietary tool, workflow-only).

note.description: Why this pick, or what to check before swapping it out.
